elements.name: 正文
elements.text: The Last Omen is an interactive visual novel set in Tang Dynasty China, built around a simple but unsettling historical fact: Princess Wencheng, one of the most celebrated women in Chinese history, never had her real name recorded.

elements.name: 文字
elements.text:
She was given away in a political marriage to the Tubo’s king Songtsen Gampo. However, no record of her real name, true intentions or thoughts has ever been found in the history books.
 
This project begins with that erasure of ancient female's agency, and asks what it might look like to give her back an interior life.

elements.name: 副标题
elements.text: a live concert where your pulse makes the world grow back ✿

elements.name: A concert wher
elements.text: A concert where the audience becomes the band. People play strange little instruments and talk to sound and animation in real time, and every note helps a "dead" landscape slowly come back to life.

elements.name: We scanned rea
elements.text:
We scanned real natural places with Luma and rebuilt them in Blender, then used Stable Diffusion to make a decayed and a regrown version of each one.

Everything runs live in TouchDesigner: pulse data from Biotronica and touch from Playtronica drive the regrowth on the projection while people play.

elements.name: Three particip
elements.text: Three participants performed live across the whole set. The bio-signal system we built became the starting point of my ongoing research on physiological input in narrative games.

elements.text:
In the 15th year of Zhenguan, the Tang Dynasty was at peace…
yet beneath all that prosperity, something no one could explain had already begun to stir.

elements.name: A teaser that
elements.text: A teaser that retells Princess Wencheng's journey to Tibet as an SCP Foundation adventure. It isn't the whole story, more a glimpse into the environments and court life, and into one woman's quiet resilience as she reshapes the fate of two cultures.

elements.name: Built from scr
elements.text: Built from scratch with a full 3D pipeline: environments and characters modelled in Blender and Maya, digital humans with MetaHuman, Tang-style court costumes sewn in Marvelous Designer following historical patterns, textures in Substance Painter, then rigged, animated, lit and rendered in Unreal Engine 5.

pages.name: The Loving of Camellia 婺界·无碍

elements.name: A barrier-free
elements.text: A barrier-free redesign proposal for People's Square in Jinhua, a square of about 46,000 m² right in the city centre that has been part of daily life for more than 50 years.

elements.name: Online researc
elements.text: Online research and fieldwork told the same story: too many bollards, no easy way in, and nothing changed for prams or wheelchairs. Ramps and steps run side by side but get cut off by columns, some ramps don't even reach the ground, and while the seating area is packed, half of the square sits empty.

elements.name: The camellia i
elements.text:
The camellia is Jinhua's city flower, voted in by locals in 1986. It means ideal, humble love, and it blooms all over the old town's carvings and paintings.

"Wu Jie" (婺界) means no boundary, "Wu Ai" (无碍) means no obstacle: a square that everyone can share.

elements.name: A camellia-sha
elements.text: A camellia-shaped floor lamp that lights the square, generates power and recycles carbon. Mist sprays softly from under the leaves, and its notched base leaves a resting spot with at least 635 × 830 mm of space for a wheelchair.

elements.name: Swim through a
elements.text: Swim through a dark maze with nothing but your own hands. A little clownfish guides you through the gloom, until the walls finally open up onto a brighter world.

elements.name: 特点
elements.text:
✋  hand-only: no controllers, no buttons, just reach, pull and glide
🌊  water that feels like water: drag and lift follow your strokes
🔊  spatial sound: listen for your guide when you can't see it
✨  and after the maze… a brighter world to explore
